text:
## Assessment Quiz  
**You must score 80%+ to pass. Questions cover:**  
1. AML screening requirements
2. KYC document validity
3. GDPR customer rights
4. Fraud red flags
5. Reporting obligations
6. Consequences of violations  
**Questions (sample):**
- Q: What should you do if a customer can't provide proof of address? A: Don't open account, escalate to manager
- Q: Can you tell a customer they matched a sanctions screen? A: No, tipping-off is illegal
- Q: How long must you keep customer data? A: 6 years after account closure
- Q: What's the Direct Debit Guarantee? A: Full refund of unauthorized DD within 10 days

raw_entities.name: AML Screening Requirements Knowledge
raw_entities.description: Staff must understand and apply AML screening requirements as assessed in the quiz, including when and how to conduct sanctions and PEP screening.
context: AML screening requirements

raw_entities.name: KYC Document Validity Assessment
raw_entities.description: Staff must be able to evaluate the validity and acceptability of KYC documents provided by customers, including proof of address requirements.
context: KYC document validity
What should you do if a customer can't provide proof of address? A: Don't open account, escalate to manager

raw_entities.name: GDPR Customer Rights Understanding
raw_entities.description: Staff must understand GDPR customer rights and data protection obligations, including data retention periods.
context: GDPR customer rights

raw_entities.name: Fraud Red Flag Recognition
raw_entities.description: Staff must be able to identify and recognize fraud red flags in customer interactions and transactions.
context: Fraud red flags

raw_entities.name: Reporting Obligations Knowledge
raw_entities.description: Staff must understand when and how to report suspicious activity and other compliance violations.
context: Reporting obligations

raw_entities.name: Consequences of Compliance Violations
raw_entities.description: Staff must understand the consequences and penalties associated with violations of AML, KYC, GDPR, and fraud prevention obligations.
context: Consequences of violations

raw_entities.name: Account Opening Refusal for Missing Proof of Address
raw_entities.description: Staff must not open an account if a customer cannot provide proof of address; instead, the request must be escalated to a manager.
context: What should you do if a customer can't provide proof of address? A: Don't open account, escalate to manager

raw_entities.name: Tipping-Off Prohibition
raw_entities.description: Staff must not inform a customer that they have matched a sanctions screen, as this constitutes illegal tipping-off under AML regulations.
context: Can you tell a customer they matched a sanctions screen? A: No, tipping-off is illegal

raw_entities.name: Customer Data Retention Requirement
raw_entities.description: Staff must retain customer data for a minimum of 6 years following account closure, as required by regulatory obligations.
context: How long must you keep customer data? A: 6 years after account closure

raw_entities.name: Customer Unable to Provide Proof of Address
raw_entities.description: A customer's inability to provide proof of address is a KYC red flag that prevents account opening and requires manager escalation.
context: What should you do if a customer can't provide proof of address? A: Don't open account, escalate to manager

raw_entities.name: Direct Debit Guarantee
raw_entities.description: A consumer protection guarantee that provides a full refund of any unauthorized direct debit payment within 10 days of discovery.
context: What's the Direct Debit Guarantee? A: Full refund of unauthorized DD within 10 days
